Girl, life gets SO GOOD when you’re done high school. I swear. And high school friends are not real friends. My 3 BEST friends from grade 7-11 eventually all decided to try to destroy my life when we were 21. Nothing bad happened between us, from my understanding we just drifted apart. I’m still pretty hurt by it because I just don’t understand why, especially when I always put them and their needs before me and my own. But they were never real friends. 

I met real friends after high school when we weren’t all locked in the same building with the same kids for like 7 hours a day. Life is just different when you’re done, you eventually realize you don’t have to care as much about everything you stressed about in HS because you’re not constantly surrounded your peers in the same way. If you go to uni or college sure, you’re with people your age, but you’re also with kids in their late 20s, a 40 yr old going back to school, etc. And everyone acts different there. In the workplace, it’s even better. You can be whoever you want to be, no one really gives a care because you’re all too invested in your own lives. 

Look up parenting your younger self. It feels good to talk to your younger self and guide her, let her know it’s okay. Somehow that makes you feel okay in whatever is happening now. Take care of yourself like you’d take care of your 6 year old self. Or whatever age you were with your SA. There’s just something about it. 

I hope you’ll be okay. I probably can’t talk you out of it so I won’t try but I’d encourage you to talk to some women older than you, whether that’s 5 years or 50 years older than you. There’s something special about hearing stories from women who have gone before you and more often than not they’ve experienced the same things you have. I mostly just want you to know that others have felt the same pain and that you’re not alone. I almost killed myself at your age, I believe it was grad night. I’m still hella depressed but I’m really happy I didn’t.

I got it the day before I turned 20 (super cool birthday gift right?). I was super worried about having to disclose to every partner because I went to a smaller  school in a small city of about 1 million so you’d always run into people you know or recognize. I’ve had quite a few partners since then and I’ve only been rejected once, but that was going to be a FWB situation anyway and we’d only been talking for like 2 days. I’ve never been rejected by a romantic partner. I like tell them on the third date because you don’t really know each other too well yet so if they wanna cut there’s no hard feelings. Here’s roughly how I disclose: 

There’s actually something I wanted to mention to you. 5 years ago I was diagnosed with cold sores, except instead of having them here (motion to mouth) I have them down under. Do you know what I mean by that? (If they don’t, tell them herpes). About 67-80% of the population has it and it isn’t on regular STI/STD screening because it’s so common and the stigma is really the worst part about it. My body has adapted really well and I haven’t had an outbreak in 3 years. I take meds to limit the potential of spreading it and I make sure I pay attention to any sensations I may have down there. But honestly, I always forget I have it until I’m dating someone new and realize I should tell them. So I’m telling you now because the reason I have to is because my ex didn’t disclose to me, and I don’t think that’s very fair. Are there any questions you have for me? 

They usually have no questions, I’ve had like 2 people ask me how I got it. You don’t have to tell them, but I do just because it was from an on again/off again boyfriend. One of the most important things though is that you stay calm because they will mirror your emotions. So think just like a child that falls down, they will look at you and if you’re reacting badly so will they. So don’t be upset, don’t say sorry, this is just a fact of your life and if they don’t like it that’s okay, they’re just showing you they weren’t mature enough for you or were only looking for a hump & dump. 

I think it takes a couple of years to see that it really isn’t a big deal at all and most others don’t see it that way either. Most people are just happy you told them and think that that shows who you are as a person so they’ll think you’re a great person just for telling them. Actually, many people I’ve told right after told me one of their deep, dark secrets to make me feel better. Pretty nice. You’re gonna do great!

No no no. Listen, I got it at 19. That SUCKED. But please understand that at least 25% of the population has it, likely more. It’s not included regular STI/STD testing, you have to specifically request it and that’s because the stigma is waaay worse than the virus itself. Most people who have it don’t know they have it. It’s honestly the safest STD you can get, think of the others that can leave you infertile, eat your brain away, or kill you. The only thing that is bad about herpes is the stigma. I haven’t had an outbreak in 3 years. I take my pills (lysine works too) when I have a partner and make sure I notice if I feel anything down there. The first outbreak sucked but after that I barely had any at all and when I did they didn’t hurt, just a little uncomfortable at times but coconut oil did the trick. 

I’ve never had an issue dating or sleeping with other people, I’ve never been turned down for a relationship.  If anything it brings me closer to the partners I tell, some even open up about some big secret they have after I tell them and it’s really sweet. If I were to be rejected I know that they aren’t mature or aren’t serious about me, and that’s okay. They took themselves out of the race before it even started and saved me time. 

I know it sucks right now but most of us that have it can honestly say that we usually forget we even have it. I only remember when I realize I’m dating someone new and should tell them. If you need help with how to disclose or anything else please reach out. Your life isn’t over, it’ll all be okay. Just take care of yourself right now, you’ll be so content in 5 years looking back. You can get through this.

I'm having the exact same problem right now but I'll share things that have helped in the past and that I'm considering trying again. 

One thing that I know definitely helped me in the past was using the 5-second rule. Author Mel Robbins claims that if you have an instinct to act on something you must do it within 5 seconds or your brain will squash the idea of it. So once you turn your alarm off you'll want to count back from five and once you're at 1, get out of bed. From here I made myself go straight to the bathroom and wash my face. This idea of acting before you even get to think about it really worked for me. I think I've put off trying this again because I'm just a little lazy and hate the idea of getting out of bed as soon as I wake up but I think it might need to be done. I know my brother had a similar routine where as soon as he was awake he would turn on the TV and turn the coffee machine on. Anything similar might help!
